objects.description: Extrajudicial killings of civilians in the course of suppressing the insurgency: the Presidium of the CPSU Central Committee itself admitted, in its resolution "On the Political and Economic Situation of the Western Oblasts of the Ukrainian SSR" of May 26, 1953: "From 1944 through 1952, up to 500 thousand people in the western oblasts of Ukraine were subjected to various kinds of repression, including over 134 thousand arrested, over 153 thousand killed, and over 203 thousand deported forever from the Ukrainian SSR"(Citation: Постановление Президиума ЦК КПСС «О политическом и хозяйственном состоянии западных областей Украинской ССР» 1953)(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004) – the authorities did not divide the killed into insurgents and civilians, and already on July 2, 1953, after Beria's arrest, the resolution itself was revoked as conducive to "the activization of bourgeois-nationalist elements"(Citation: Постановление Президиума ЦК КПСС «О политическом и хозяйственном состоянии западных областей Украинской ССР» 1953). Terror was also waged by disguised MGB "special groups" acting under the guise of the UPA: the military prosecutor of the MVD troops of the Ukrainian district, Kosharsky, in his report to Khrushchev (February 15, 1949), cited "examples of beatings, rapes and robberies of the population" by agent-fighters and stated: "the actions of the so-called MGB special groups are of a pronounced bandit, anti-Soviet character and, of course, cannot be justified by any operational considerations"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011).

objects.description: Extrajudicial killings of civilians in the course of suppressing the insurgency: the Presidium of the CPSU Central Committee itself admitted, in its resolution "On the Political and Economic Situation of the Western Oblasts of the Ukrainian SSR" of May 26, 1953: "From 1944 through 1952, up to 500 thousand people in the western oblasts of Ukraine were subjected to various kinds of repression, including over 134 thousand arrested, over 153 thousand killed, and over 203 thousand deported forever from the Ukrainian SSR"(Citation: Постановление Президиума ЦК КПСС «О политическом и хозяйственном состоянии западных областей Украинской ССР» 1953)(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004) – the authorities did not divide the killed into insurgents and civilians, and already on July 2, 1953, after Beria's arrest, the resolution itself was revoked as conducive to "the activization of bourgeois-nationalist elements"(Citation: Постановление Президиума ЦК КПСС «О политическом и хозяйственном состоянии западных областей Украинской ССР» 1953). Terror was also waged by disguised MGB "special groups" acting under the guise of the UPA: the military prosecutor of the MVD troops of the Ukrainian district, Kosharsky, in his report to Khrushchev (February 15, 1949), cited "examples of beatings, rapes and robberies of the population" by agent-fighters and stated: "the actions of the so-called MGB special groups are of a pronounced bandit, anti-Soviet character and, of course, cannot be justified by any operational considerations"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 8 2011).

objects.description: The creation of an atmosphere of total fear through the bloody provocations of NKVD special groups operating in the guise of the UPA: People's Commissar Strokach "initiated the formation of special groups of the NKVD of the Ukrainian SSR from former partisans for the struggle against the UPA" and "personally interrogated the captured leaders of the OUN networks of Western Ukraine"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 9 2012). The terror was also demonstrative: "one of the forms of struggle was the policy of intimidating OUN and UPA members and the local population: open trials and executions, putting the bodies of the dead on public display, and destroying insurgent graves"(Citation: Рух Опору у Карпатському краї (1940–1950 рр.): тексти лекцій (Ільницький) 2024).

objects.description: The forcible removal of insurgents' families to Siberia and the deportation of the Ukrainians of Zakerzonnia: the removal of "bandit accomplices" with their entire families began at once - already in the summer of 1944 "more than 17,000 people were carried off to Krasnoyarsk Krai"(Citation: Депортація (Енциклопедія Сучасної України) 2007); in all, in 1944–52, 203,662 people were removed to special settlements, among them "representatives of the families of members of the Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists and soldiers of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army and their sympathizers — 182,543 people"(Citation: Депортація (Енциклопедія Сучасної України) 2007). Operation "Vistula" was carried out in order to "deprive it of socio-economic and moral-psychological support from the local Ukrainian population," and ended in the scattering of the community: the authorities rid themselves of the Ukrainian population, "dispersing about 150 thousand people"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003).

objects.description: Mass arrests of UPA fighters, OUN members, and those suspected of aiding them, followed by dispatch to the GULAG camps, upon which the regime placed "the isolation of 'unreliable elements'" as one of its key tasks(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 2 2004). During Operation "Vistula," for civilians suspected of assisting the underground there was provision for "the introduction of courts-martial and concentration camps, in particular at Jaworzno"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Т. 1 2003). By 1951 Ukrainians had become the second-largest nation of the GULAG: according to the agency's own statistics, the "National composition of GULAG prisoners (as of January 1, 1951)" counted 506,221 Ukrainians out of some 2.5 million prisoners - about 20%(Citation: ГУЛАГ (историко-социологический аспект) (Земсков) 1991).

objects.description: The redrawing of internal borders by the USSR Supreme Soviet Presidium's resolution of 19 February 1954: "To approve the joint submission of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the RSFSR and the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the Ukrainian SSR on the transfer of the Crimean oblast from the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic to the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic"(Citation: Указ о передаче Крымской области из состава РСФСР в состав УССР 1954) – the decision was taken in Moscow, without any expression of will by the peninsula's inhabitants. Behind the "commonality of the economy" stood the desire to shift the peninsula, ruined by deportation and war, onto the books of the Ukrainian SSR: "Moscow admits ever more openly: the Crimean region is a problem territory that the union center does not know how to sustain"(Citation: Подарунок Хрущова — Крим у складі Української РСР — що насправді відбулося у 1954 році (Суспільне) 2026).

objects.description: The jubilee was fixed with a material sign in Pereiaslav in the Kyiv region, on the very square where the rada had taken place in 1654. The sign went up in the course of the jubilee reconstruction of the town ordered by the republic's authorities: "in connection with the preparation for the celebration of the 300th anniversary of the reunification of Ukraine with Russia," the Council of Ministers of the Ukrainian SSR allocated 20 million rubles for the reconstruction of Pereiaslav-Khmelnytskyi, the reconstruction plan was developed under the direction of the architect Volodymyr Zabolotnyi, and in May 1954, "on the square where the historic Pereiaslav Rada took place (now Reunification Square), an obelisk with a memorial plaque was erected"(Citation: Історія міст і сіл Української РСР. Київська область 1971). On the plaque, beneath a relief of Bohdan Khmelnytsky, a text is cast: "On this square, on 8 (18) January 1654, the Pereiaslav Rada took place, which, expressing the will of the Ukrainian people, unanimously adopted the historic decision on the reunification of Ukraine with Russia"(Citation: Пам'ятний знак на честь 300-річчя Переяславської Ради, обеліск на площі Переяславської Ради 2014). The sign did not merely mark the spot: it declared the decision unanimous and expressive of the people's will, fixing this version in bronze on the very square where it all happened.

objects.description: The use of brute force by party activists against Rukh activists: when Rukh members attempted to install a cross on the grave of those executed near Bazar, "the activists were not allowed into the village" "with the help of KGB men and provocations about the Rukh members' 'Banderite' intentions"; some participants "were dragged out of the car, beaten, and the flags were torn to shreds," while the role of "protesting peasants" was played by men in disguise: "in reality these were communist party activists from nearby districts"(Citation: Брав участь у спробі вшанувати Героїв Базару (MALYN.MEDIA) 2023). The political prisoner Vasyl Ovsienko ended up in the hospital: "the communists thrashed me near Bazar on November 17"(Citation: Інтерв'ю Василя Овсієнка (Музей дисидентського руху) 2011).

The political prisoner Vasyl Ovsienko ended up in the hospital: "the communists thrashed me near Bazar on November 17"(Citation: Інтерв'ю Василя Овсієнка (Музей дисидентського руху) 2011).

objects.description: The forced disappearance of a key functionary of the movement: "on the night of January 15–16, 1994, two armed unknown men burst into the NRU secretariat in Kyiv, took some documents, and searched for Boichyshyn" - Mykhailo Boichyshyn, head of the Rukh secretariat, was never seen again. The investigation was sabotaged: law enforcement "at first was in no hurry to accept the report of the politician's disappearance, and then demonstratively displayed disinterest in solving the crime," and "the investigators were interested not so much in the circumstances of the attack on the Secretariat and Boichyshyn's disappearance as in the party's financing"(Citation: Михайло Бойчишин — голова Секретаріату НРУ (Український погляд) 2024).

The investigation was sabotaged: law enforcement "at first was in no hurry to accept the report of the politician's disappearance, and then demonstratively displayed disinterest in solving the crime," and "the investigators were interested not so much in the circumstances of the attack on the Secretariat and Boichyshyn's disappearance as in the party's financing"(Citation: Михайло Бойчишин — голова Секретаріату НРУ (Український погляд) 2024).

objects.description: An armed seizure of power: the GKChP statement of 18 August 1991 announced the transfer of the USSR president's powers: "In connection with the impossibility, for reasons of health, of Mikhail Sergeevich Gorbachev performing the duties of President of the USSR and the transfer… of the powers of the President of the USSR to Vice-President Gennady Ivanovich Yanayev… to form the State Committee for the State of Emergency in the USSR"(Citation: Заявление ГКЧП 1991). The putsch was timed to derail the treaty-based reconstitution of the Union: "The formation of the GKChP was preceded by the so-called Novo-Ogaryovo process - negotiations begun on April 23, 1991 by USSR President Gorbachev at his suburban residence of Novo-Ogaryovo with the leaders of the union republics on the signing of a new Union Treaty"(Citation: Енциклопедія історії України: Додатковий том 2021) - the coup cut this process short.

objects.description: An attempt to physically eliminate the leader of the democratic opposition V. Yushchenko at the height of the election campaign by dioxin poisoning: in late December 2004 "a patient presented with TCDD poisoning; the levels in his blood serum (108000 pg/g lipid weight) were more than 50 000-fold greater than those in the general population"(Citation: TCDD poisoning in Victor Yushchenko (The Lancet) 2009). The poisoning led to severe disfigurement of the candidate's face.

That is, Ukraine's economy is developing in a diversified way"(Citation: Прямая линия с жителями Украины 2004). In parallel, opponents were demonized with accusations of nationalism and pro-fascist views.

objects.description: The imposition of corrupt gas-supply schemes through intermediary companies: Moscow "used a series of intermediary trading companies (Itera from 1998, Eural Trans Gas from 2003, Rosukrenergo (RUE) from 2005) to transport, and sometimes to supply, the gas to Ukraine," a practice that "was long criticized in European government circles and by corporate governance bodies (where there was concern about their opacity)"(Citation: The Russo-Ukrainian gas dispute of January 2009 2009). RUE's co-owner Dmytro Firtash told the US ambassador in December 2008 outright that "He acknowledged ties to Russian organized crime figure Seymon Mogilevich, stating he needed Mogilevich's approval to get into business in the first place"(Citation: Cable 08KYIV2414: Firtash makes his case to the USG 2008).

objects.description: An attempt to strike a deal with the US leader over Kyiv's head in order to block Ukraine's Euro-Atlantic integration under the threat of its dismemberment: Ukraine's accession to NATO would create "a field of conflict for you and us, long-term confrontation," while Moscow, relying on anti-NATO forces, "would be working on stripping NATO of the possibility of enlarging. Russia would be creating problems there all the time"(Citation: Memorandum of Conversation: Meeting with President of Russia (Sochi) 2008). As retold by Kommersant's source from the summit itself: "You understand, George, that Ukraine is not even a state! What is Ukraine? Part of its territory is Eastern Europe, and part - a considerable part - was gifted by us!" - with a transparent hint "that Russia could begin the severance of Crimea and Eastern Ukraine"(Citation: Блок НАТО разошелся на блокпакеты (Коммерсантъ) 2008).

Russia would be creating problems there all the time"(Citation: Memorandum of Conversation: Meeting with President of Russia (Sochi) 2008). As retold by Kommersant's source from the summit itself: "You understand, George, that Ukraine is not even a state! What is Ukraine? Part of its territory is Eastern Europe, and part - a considerable part - was gifted by us!" - with a transparent hint "that Russia could begin the severance of Crimea and Eastern Ukraine"(Citation: Блок НАТО разошелся на блокпакеты (Коммерсантъ) 2008).

objects.description: The use of economic blackmail and promises of a loan together with a gas discount to coerce V. Yanukovych into derailing the signing of the Association Agreement with the EU: on December 17, 2013, a reduction of the gas price "to 268.5 dollars per thousand cubic meters" (instead of 410) was announced, along with the fact that "Ukraine, under the bilateral agreements, will receive 15 billion dollars from the Russian National Welfare Fund, selling Moscow its government securities for that amount." Putin stressed: "We consider this a temporary solution, bearing in mind that long-term, long-lasting agreements must and will be reached"(Citation: Виктор Янукович и Владимир Путин достигли компромисса в Москве 2013).

objects.description: The use of regular troops without insignia to establish control over the peninsula. A year later V. Putin admitted it on his call-in show of 17 April 2014: "behind the backs of Crimea's self-defense forces, our servicemen, of course, stood. They acted very correctly, but… decisively and professionally"(Citation: Прямая линия с Владимиром Путиным 2014). Ukrainian garrisons on the peninsula were blockaded and disarmed, as Putin himself admitted: "and the way the Ukrainian units were disarmed - all of this was done so swiftly that it seemed it had been prepared for an incredibly long time"(Citation: Прямая линия с Владимиром Путиным 2014).

objects.description: The installation of a controlled administration under military cover: the decisions of the Crimean parliament were taken in conditions where "behind the backs of Crimea's self-defense forces, our servicemen, of course, stood"(Citation: Прямая линия с Владимиром Путиным 2014). The UN General Assembly declared the ensuing referendum void and confirmed that it "was not authorized by Ukraine"(Citation: Territorial integrity of Ukraine (A/RES/68/262) 2014). OHCHR recorded the "election" scene itself: overnight into 27 February "armed groups without insignia took over the buildings of the local government and parliament," and "on 27 February, members of the Parliament of Crimea, in the presence of gunmen, dismissed the local Government and elected Sergey Aksenov as the Head of Crimea"(Citation: Situation of human rights in the temporarily occupied Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol (OHCHR) 2017).

objects.description: The seizure of Sloviansk by an armed group that had crossed the border, and the formation of the separatist "DNR"/"LNR": the detachment's commander openly admitted that "in practice it was our detachment that set in motion the flywheel of the war that is still going on," and that "it was I, after all, who pulled the trigger of the war"(Citation: Стрелков: Спусковой крючок войны нажал я 2014). In parallel, "groups of armed men unlawfully carried out a well-organized and coordinated seizure of public buildings and police and security service offices"(Citation: Доклад Верховного комиссара ООН по правам человека о положении в области прав человека в Украине (A/HRC/27/75) 2014). The "republic's" leadership was from the outset dispatched from Moscow: "Alexander Boroday - the first prime minister of the DNR, who in 2014 handed over his powers to Alexander Zakharchenko," a Muscovite raised "in an intelligentsia Moscow family"(Citation: Александр Бородай: я могу вернуться, но не на Донбасс, а уже в Киев (АиФ) 2016).

objects.description: A massive campaign of fabricating fakes to dehumanize Ukrainians: on state television it was claimed that "Ukrainian armed forces herded city residents to the central square and publicly executed a small boy and his mother," yet "there is no evidence to support Pyshniak's claim," and the residents of Sloviansk who were interviewed did not confirm the story(Citation: Fake: Crucifixion in Slovyansk 2014). The same method produced the fabricated "death of a 10-year-old girl" in the Petrovskyi district of Donetsk (March 2015): BBC correspondents on the ground established that no such girl had ever existed(Citation: Би Би Си разоблачили ложь российских СМИ о якобы погибшей 10-летней девочке (StopFake) 2015). In parallel ran an operation to conceal responsibility for the destruction of flight MH17: the Russian Ministry of Defense "made a series of self-contradictory claims blaming Ukraine, rather than Russia or Russian-led separatists, for the Boeing 777's shoot down," while a deputy defense minister publicly repeated "a fabricated claim that originated on Twitter of how a Spanish air traffic controller named Carlos saw two Ukrainian fighter jets near MH17"(Citation: The Kremlin's Shifting, Self-Contradicting Narratives on MH17 2019).

external_references.description: StopFake. (2014). Fake: Crucifixion in Slovyansk.

objects.description: The use of a hacker group linked to the security services to compromise Ukrainian artillerymen's software: "the filename 'Попр-Д30.apk' was linked to a legitimate application which was initially developed domestically within Ukraine by an officer of the 55th Artillery Brigade named Yaroslav Sherstuk," and "in-depth reverse engineering revealed the APK contained an Android variant of X-Agent" - an implant whose exclusive operator is FANCY BEAR(Citation: Danger Close: Fancy Bear Tracking of Ukrainian Field Artillery Units 2016). The same toolkit was used in cyberattacks on the Ukrainian power grid in the winters of 2015 and 2016(Citation: 2015 Ukraine Electric Power Attack | MITRE ATT&CK® 2023)(Citation: 2016 Ukraine Electric Power Attack | MITRE ATT&CK® 2023).

objects.description: The overt crossing of the state border by regular Russian troops in the summer and autumn of 2014 to save the separatists from defeat: the "DNR" commander admitted that the decisive role was played by Russian servicemen who came "on leave" - "it was mostly 'vacationers' who advanced on Mariupol. When they left, both the front line and the opportunities became precarious"(Citation: Стрелков: Спусковой крючок войны нажал я 2014). The offensive resulted in heavy losses for the Ukrainian army near Ilovaisk and Debaltseve. The presence of regular troops continued into 2015: the GRU men captured near Shchastia were "soldiers of the 3rd Separate Guards Special Purpose Brigade of the Main Directorate of the General Staff of the Russian Armed Forces, who arrived on the territory of Ukraine on March 26 and were quartered in Luhansk"(Citation: «Короче, разведка — россияне». Как искали, судили и защищали капитана Ерофеева и сержанта Александрова (Медиазона) 2016).

When they left, both the front line and the opportunities became precarious"(Citation: Стрелков: Спусковой крючок войны нажал я 2014). The offensive resulted in heavy losses for the Ukrainian army near Ilovaisk and Debaltseve. The presence of regular troops continued into 2015: the GRU men captured near Shchastia were "soldiers of the 3rd Separate Guards Special Purpose Brigade of the Main Directorate of the General Staff of the Russian Armed Forces, who arrived on the territory of Ukraine on March 26 and were quartered in Luhansk"(Citation: «Короче, разведка — россияне». Как искали, судили и защищали капитана Ерофеева и сержанта Александрова (Медиазона) 2016).

objects.description: An attempted armed seizure of power in the spring of 2014 by storming regional administrations: the UN recorded that already "in mid-April 2014" "groups of armed men unlawfully carried out a well-organized and coordinated seizure of public buildings and police and security service offices in towns and villages of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions," and "in order to retain control of the seized areas these groups erected barricades and checkpoints"(Citation: Доклад Верховного комиссара ООН по правам человека о положении в области прав человека в Украине (A/HRC/27/75) 2014). In Kharkiv the coup was quickly suppressed.

objects.description: The instigation of armed clashes in Odesa on May 2, 2014: the UN records the violence committed "in Odesa on 2 May 2014 during clashes between supporters of unity and supporters of the federalization of Ukraine, as a result of which 48 people died, mostly supporters of the country's federalization," and notes that "no one has yet been held to account"(Citation: Доклад Верховного комиссара ООН по правам человека о положении в области прав человека в Украине (A/HRC/27/75) 2014). The culmination was the fire in the Trade Union Building where activists had taken refuge: the UN monitoring mission listed among the key uninvestigated questions "what caused the fire in the Trade Union building" and "who are the perpetrators of the killings"(Citation: Report on the human rights situation in Ukraine, 15 June 2014 (OHCHR) 2014).

objects.description: The use of armed formations to seize Mariupol in the spring and summer of 2014: as the "DNR" commander admitted, "it was mostly 'vacationers' who advanced on Mariupol" - that is, Russian servicemen - and after their departure "both the front line and the opportunities became precarious"(Citation: Стрелков: Спусковой крючок войны нажал я 2014). The attempt to establish control over the city failed - on June 13 it was retaken by Ukrainian forces.

objects.description: The exploitation of the Odesa tragedy to build a state propaganda myth and invert the roles: the actual picture, per the UN, is clashes "between supporters of unity and supporters of the federalization of Ukraine, as a result of which 48 people died," while the investigation remains incomplete and "no one has yet been held to account"(Citation: Доклад Верховного комиссара ООН по правам человека о положении в области прав человека в Украине (A/HRC/27/75) 2014). The tragedy was used as moral justification for further aggression - by the same device as the "crucified boy" fake, for which "there is no evidence to support Pyshniak's claim"(Citation: Fake: Crucifixion in Slovyansk 2014).

external_references.source_name: Доклад Верховного комиссара ООН по правам человека о положении в области прав человека в Украине (A/HRC/27/75) 2014
external_references.description: УВКПЛ ООН. (2014). Доклад Верховного комиссара ООН по правам человека о положении в области прав человека в Украине (A/HRC/27/75).
StopFake. (2014). Fake: Crucifixion in Slovyansk.

objects.description: The exploitation of the Odesa tragedy to build a state propaganda myth and invert the roles: the actual picture, per the UN, is clashes "between supporters of unity and supporters of the federalization of Ukraine, as a result of which 48 people died," while the investigation remains incomplete and "no one has yet been held to account"(Citation: Доклад Верховного комиссара ООН по правам человека о положении в области прав человека в Украине (A/HRC/27/75) 2014). The tragedy was used as moral justification for further aggression - by the same device as the "crucified boy" fake, for which "there is no evidence to support Pyshniak's claim"(Citation: Fake: Crucifixion in Slovyansk 2014).

objects.description: The publication of the manifesto "On the Historical Unity of Russians and Ukrainians" (July 2021), constructing a pseudo-historical myth: "Russians and Ukrainians are one people, a single whole," while modern borders are declared the result of the fact that "the Bolsheviks' actions in severing from Russia its historical territories are not considered a criminal act"(Citation: Статья Владимира Путина «Об историческом единстве русских и украинцев» 2021). The same article describes how Lenin personally "persuaded" the leaders of the Donetsk-Kryvyi Rih republic "to act within Soviet Ukraine," and how the Central Committee resolved "to create at the congress 'one government for all of Ukraine'"(Citation: Статья Владимира Путина «Об историческом единстве русских и украинцев» 2021). On the eve of the invasion the thesis was taken to its limit: in his address of February 21, 2022 Putin declared that "modern Ukraine was entirely and wholly created by Russia, or, to be more precise, by Bolshevik, communist Russia," and called the country "Ukraine named after Vladimir Ilyich Lenin" - "He is its author and architect"(Citation: Обращение Президента Российской Федерации 21 февраля 2022 года 2022).

objects.description: An article by D. Medvedev, deputy chairman of Russia's Security Council, in Kommersant (11 October 2021) marginalizing the Ukrainian leadership: "it is pointless for us to deal with vassals. One must do business with the suzerain"; "at the head of Ukraine stand weak people who strive only to line their own pockets," and negotiations with them are "absolutely pointless"(Citation: Почему бессмысленны контакты с нынешним украинским руководством 2021). In the same text the Ukrainian president was likened to a hypothetical Jew serving in the SS(Citation: Почему бессмысленны контакты с нынешним украинским руководством 2021).

objects.description: An article by D. Medvedev, deputy chairman of Russia's Security Council, in Kommersant (11 October 2021) marginalizing the Ukrainian leadership: "it is pointless for us to deal with vassals. One must do business with the suzerain"; "at the head of Ukraine stand weak people who strive only to line their own pockets," and negotiations with them are "absolutely pointless"(Citation: Почему бессмысленны контакты с нынешним украинским руководством 2021). In the same text the Ukrainian president was likened to a hypothetical Jew serving in the SS(Citation: Почему бессмысленны контакты с нынешним украинским руководством 2021).

objects.description: The deliberate killing of civilians in occupied territories: the UN commission established "a widespread pattern of summary executions in areas that the armed forces of the Russian Federation controlled in 17 localities of Chernihiv, Kharkiv, Kyiv and Sumy Provinces, with the highest number in Kyiv Province, including in the city of Bucha," confirming "the execution of 65 men, 2 women and a 14-year-old boy"; "in more than half of the executions investigated, witnesses had last seen the victims in the custody of the armed forces of the Russian Federation"(Citation: Report of the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine (A/HRC/52/62) 2023).

objects.description: The practice of "urbicide" - the deliberate erasure of entire Ukrainian cities (for example, Mariupol), the destruction of infrastructure, and the entombment of the dead in the foundations of ruins(Citation: Рашизм: Звір з безодні 2023). The blowing up of the Kakhovka dam on 6 June 2023: "the breach of the dam at the Kakhovska Hydroelectric Power Plant in June 2023 resulted in massive flooding downstream, triggering an environmental disaster that has already had catastrophic effects on communities across the region," while "the flooding killed 34 civilians (32 in Kherson region and 2 in Mykolaiv region)" on Ukrainian-controlled territory alone(Citation: Report on the human rights situation in Ukraine, 1 February to 31 July 2023 (OHCHR) 2023). The scale of the disaster on the very first day: "about 16 thousand people on the right bank of Kherson region are in the critical zone," with 80 settlements under threat of flooding(Citation: Підрив Каховської ГЕС: близько 16 тисяч людей на правому березі Дніпра в критичній зоні (NV) 2023).

The blowing up of the Kakhovka dam on 6 June 2023: "the breach of the dam at the Kakhovska Hydroelectric Power Plant in June 2023 resulted in massive flooding downstream, triggering an environmental disaster that has already had catastrophic effects on communities across the region," while "the flooding killed 34 civilians (32 in Kherson region and 2 in Mykolaiv region)" on Ukrainian-controlled territory alone(Citation: Report on the human rights situation in Ukraine, 1 February to 31 July 2023 (OHCHR) 2023). objects.description: Nuclear blackmail and the armed seizure of nuclear facilities: the IAEA recorded that "a large number of Russian tanks and infantry 'broke through the block-post' to the town of Enerhodar, a few kilometres from the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant," while the Ukrainian regulator reported that "Russian infantry troops were moving directly towards the site of Ukraine's largest nuclear power plant," calling the situation "critical"(Citation: IAEA Director General Statement on Situation in Ukraine, Update 9 2022). International bodies also voiced concern about "the unacceptable nuclear rhetoric used by Russian officials"(Citation: Report of the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine (A/HRC/52/62) 2023). Already on February 24 the Chornobyl NPP was seized as well: Ukraine informed the IAEA that "Russian forces had taken control of the facilities of the State Specialized Enterprise Chornobyl NPP" within the Exclusion Zone(Citation: Update 4 – IAEA Director General Statement on Situation in Ukraine 2022).

objects.description: The mass deportation and forcible transfer of Ukrainian children: the International Criminal Court established responsibility for "the war crime of unlawful deportation of population (children) and that of unlawful transfer of population (children) from occupied areas of Ukraine to the Russian Federation"(Citation: ICC judges issue arrest warrants against Vladimir Putin and Maria Lvova-Belova 2023), issuing arrest warrants against Putin personally and against the commissioner for children's rights Maria Lvova-Belova. The large-scale plunder of the economic resources of the occupied territories: "from 2022 to 2025, almost 15 million tonnes of Ukrainian grain, valued at 6.8 billion US dollars, were illegally removed from the temporarily occupied districts of Ukraine"(Citation: Росія вивезла майже 15 млн тонн українського зерна з окупованих територій 2026). Strikes on port infrastructure were accompanied by "the destruction of grain and other products destined for export"(Citation: Report on the human rights situation in Ukraine, 1 February to 31 July 2023 (OHCHR) 2023). The plunder extended to industry: "the owners of the stolen metal - the Azovstal, MMKI and Zaporizhstal plants - have already filed a series of criminal complaints"(Citation: Викрадаючи український метал, Росія скоює міжнародний воєнний злочин – "Метінвест" (Gordon) 2022).

The Council of Europe characterizes these attacks on cultural heritage as having a "genocidal dimension"(Citation: Ukraine's Stolen Art: Cultural plunder in the shadow of war 2025).

objects.description: From April 2022 the Russian occupation administrations marked the seized territories with imperial signs - in stone and on paper. In Kherson oblast more than 110 Lenin monuments had been dismantled before the invasion, with practically none left; after the occupation the invaders erected ten new ones: the first in Henichesk in April 2022 - the first Lenin monument on Ukrainian territory since 2014 - and at the end of that same month a monument was returned to its pedestal by the city council in Nova Kakhovka(Citation: Ідеологія в бронзі: навіщо Росія «засіває» окуповану Херсонщину своїми монументами 2026). In Mariupol on 5 May 2022 a monument to a woman with a red flag was unveiled, and the ceremony was published in his Telegram channel by Andrei Turchak, secretary of the general council of "United Russia"; the Square of the Warrior-Liberators, named in honor of those who freed the city from the Nazis, was given back its Soviet name of "Lenin Komsomol Square" by the occupiers(Citation: У Маріуполі окупанти встановили пам'ятник «бабці з червоною ганчіркою» 2022). In parallel the occupation administration papered the territory with banners: in Kherson and Nova Kakhovka hung Russian-language billboards reading "Russia is here forever!," "Kherson - forever with Russia," "Kherson is a Russian city," and for them they bought, for twenty cents on a stock-photo site, a picture by the Ukrainian photographer Anna Pasichnyk - her son Yaroslav with a friend in vyshyvankas in a rapeseed field near Kyiv - painting a Russian flag in behind the children's backs(Citation: Украинка обнаружила свою фотографию с детьми в вышиванках на билборде в поддержку аннексии Херсона 2022). In Balakliia in Kharkiv oblast the occupiers pasted over a city banner: first they hung "Ukraine and Russia are 'one'" on top of it, then a poster with a tricolor reading "We are one people with Russia!". On 10 September 2022 Ukrainian soldiers tore the tricolor down - and beneath it emerged the lines of Shevchenko that had stood there through the entire occupation: "Fight - and you shall prevail! God is helping you! Truth is with you, glory is with you, and holy freedom!"(Citation: «Борітеся - поборете»: історія плаката з рядками Шевченка, який росіяни заклеїли під час окупації Балаклії 2023). The signs held only until de-occupation: on 11 November 2022, a "Russia is here forever" poster in liberated Bilozerka in the Kherson region was torn down by local residents - the video was published by the Telegram channel "Nikolaevsky Vanek"(Citation: В освобожденной Белозерке Херсонской области срывают плакаты «Россия здесь навсегда» 2022).

In Kherson oblast more than 110 Lenin monuments had been dismantled before the invasion, with practically none left; after the occupation the invaders erected ten new ones: the first in Henichesk in April 2022 - the first Lenin monument on Ukrainian territory since 2014 - and at the end of that same month a monument was returned to its pedestal by the city council in Nova Kakhovka(Citation: Ідеологія в бронзі: навіщо Росія «засіває» окуповану Херсонщину своїми монументами 2026). In Mariupol on 5 May 2022 a monument to a woman with a red flag was unveiled, and the ceremony was published in his Telegram channel by Andrei Turchak, secretary of the general council of "United Russia"; the Square of the Warrior-Liberators, named in honor of those who freed the city from the Nazis, was given back its Soviet name of "Lenin Komsomol Square" by the occupiers(Citation: У Маріуполі окупанти встановили пам'ятник «бабці з червоною ганчіркою» 2022). In parallel the occupation administration papered the territory with banners: in Kherson and Nova Kakhovka hung Russian-language billboards reading "Russia is here forever!," "Kherson - forever with Russia," "Kherson is a Russian city," and for them they bought, for twenty cents on a stock-photo site, a picture by the Ukrainian photographer Anna Pasichnyk - her son Yaroslav with a friend in vyshyvankas in a rapeseed field near Kyiv - painting a Russian flag in behind the children's backs(Citation: Украинка обнаружила свою фотографию с детьми в вышиванках на билборде в поддержку аннексии Херсона 2022). In Balakliia in Kharkiv oblast the occupiers pasted over a city banner: first they hung "Ukraine and Russia are 'one'" on top of it, then a poster with a tricolor reading "We are one people with Russia!". On 10 September 2022 Ukrainian soldiers tore the tricolor down - and beneath it emerged the lines of Shevchenko that had stood there through the entire occupation: "Fight - and you shall prevail! God is helping you! Truth is with you, glory is with you, and holy freedom!"(Citation: «Борітеся - поборете»: історія плаката з рядками Шевченка, який росіяни заклеїли під час окупації Балаклії 2023). The signs held only until de-occupation: on 11 November 2022, a "Russia is here forever" poster in liberated Bilozerka in the Kherson region was torn down by local residents - the video was published by the Telegram channel "Nikolaevsky Vanek"(Citation: В освобожденной Белозерке Херсонской области срывают плакаты «Россия здесь навсегда» 2022).

objects.description: The government of the Tsardom of Muscovy used religious identity and the concept of protecting co-religionists as ideological cover for military expansion: historian Michael Khodarkovsky states that the diplomatic apparatus positioned the tsar as a "universal Christian ruler who 'upheld the true Christian faith'"(Citation: Russia's Steppe Frontier: The Making of a Colonial Empire 1500-1800 2002), while invasions were motivated by a "divine obligation to rescue Orthodox Christians from infidel captivity"(Citation: Russia's Steppe Frontier: The Making of a Colonial Empire 1500-1800 2002); as a result, as historian Michael Khodarkovsky summarizes, in the advance into new territories "Moscow's military and political interests could no longer be separated from the ideological and theological rhetoric of expansion"(Citation: Russia's Steppe Frontier: The Making of a Colonial Empire 1500-1800 2002), because of which the North Caucasus "became a religious frontier"(Citation: Of Christianity, Enlightenment, and Colonialism: Russia in the North Caucasus, 1550–1800 1999).

objects.description: The government of the Tsardom of Muscovy used religious identity and the concept of protecting co-religionists as ideological cover for military expansion: historian Michael Khodarkovsky states that the diplomatic apparatus positioned the tsar as a "universal Christian ruler who 'upheld the true Christian faith'"(Citation: Russia's Steppe Frontier: The Making of a Colonial Empire 1500-1800 2002), while invasions were motivated by a "divine obligation to rescue Orthodox Christians from infidel captivity"(Citation: Russia's Steppe Frontier: The Making of a Colonial Empire 1500-1800 2002); as a result, as historian Michael Khodarkovsky summarizes, in the advance into new territories "Moscow's military and political interests could no longer be separated from the ideological and theological rhetoric of expansion"(Citation: Russia's Steppe Frontier: The Making of a Colonial Empire 1500-1800 2002), because of which the North Caucasus "became a religious frontier"(Citation: Of Christianity, Enlightenment, and Colonialism: Russia in the North Caucasus, 1550–1800 1999).

objects.description: The government of the Tsardom of Muscovy fabricated historical narratives to provide legal justification for the invasion of new territories: historian Michael Khodarkovsky points out that in diplomatic correspondence officials deliberately constructed fictitious claims that the Indigenous peoples of the Caucasus had allegedly, since ancient times, been Muscovite "subjects in the Riazan region, who then fled from Riazan and settled in the mountains"(Citation: Russia's Steppe Frontier: The Making of a Colonial Empire 1500-1800 2002).

Babichev and P. Protasyev were dispatched from Moscow "with many men, as well as ordnance, cannons, and arquebuses"(Citation: Народы Северного Кавказа и их связи с Россией (вторая половина XVI - 30-е годы XVII вв) 1963), while historians A. S. Kulikov and V. A. Runov note that they were sent "with firepower and many men"(Citation: Все Кавказские войны России. Самая полная энциклопедия 2013).

objects.description: The military forces of the Tsardom of Muscovy repeatedly rebuilt the fortified outpost on the lands of the Nokhchi: historian E. N. Kusheva writes that "in 1577 - 1578... the Russian town was reestablished on the Terek River at the mouth of the Sunzha"(Citation: Народы Северного Кавказа и их связи с Россией (вторая половина XVI - 30-е годы XVII вв) 1963), while the compiler of the collection of documents E. N. Kusheva indicates that the military forces of the Tsardom of Muscovy "rebuilt the ostrog in 1590 and 1635"(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997) and that "in 1651 a Russian ostrog was built anew on the left bank of the Sunzha"(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

objects.description: The military forces of the Tsardom of Muscovy repeatedly rebuilt the fortified outpost on the lands of the Nokhchi: historian E. N. Kusheva writes that "in 1577 - 1578... the Russian town was reestablished on the Terek River at the mouth of the Sunzha"(Citation: Народы Северного Кавказа и их связи с Россией (вторая половина XVI - 30-е годы XVII вв) 1963), while the compiler of the collection of documents E. N. Kusheva indicates that the military forces of the Tsardom of Muscovy "rebuilt the ostrog in 1590 and 1635"(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997) and that "in 1651 a Russian ostrog was built anew on the left bank of the Sunzha"(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

objects.description: The occupation administration of the Tsardom of Muscovy systematically brought armed detachments into the lands of the Nokhchi to hold the bridgehead: the compiler of the collection of documents E. N. Kusheva indicates that at the site of the fortress, "by order of the Terek voivodes, a detachment of streltsy and Cossacks was permanently stationed"(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997), and during the siege of 1653 it held "Russian service men, Terek atamans, and Cossacks"(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

objects.description: The military forces of the Tsardom of Muscovy erected a new fortified base: historian E. N. Kusheva writes that they «were building it in 1588-1589... Mikhailo Burtsev and Kelar Protasyev... the main force of its garrison consisted of streltsy armed with «fire weaponry», with pishchal arquebuses»(Citation: Народы Северного Кавказа и их связи с Россией (вторая половина XVI - 30-е годы XVII вв) 1963), while historians A. S. Kulikov and V. A. Runov add that in the early 17th century «the Terek fort had turned into a rather powerful fortress. Its artillery numbered 40 large guns»(Citation: Все Кавказские войны России. Самая полная энциклопедия 2013).

objects.description: A permanent military contingent maintained at state expense was stationed in the territory: historian I. Kh. Tkhamokova quotes a tsar's decree according to which «in 1623, «upon the petition of the Terek and Greben Cossacks», a tsar's decree was sent to the Terek ordering the payment of salaries to 30 atamans and 470 rank-and-file Cossacks»(Citation: Терское казачество в этнокультурном пространстве Северного Кавказа 2017). New personnel were also sent in to hold the positions: historian I. Kh. Tkhamokova notes that «in 1589, soon after the town was built, 800 streltsy and Cossacks were to be sent there from Astrakhan, but the Astrakhan voivode sent only 600 men»(Citation: Терское казачество в этнокультурном пространстве Северного Кавказа 2017).

Tkhamokova quotes a tsar's decree according to which «in 1623, «upon the petition of the Terek and Greben Cossacks», a tsar's decree was sent to the Terek ordering the payment of salaries to 30 atamans and 470 rank-and-file Cossacks»(Citation: Терское казачество в этнокультурном пространстве Северного Кавказа 2017). New personnel were also sent in to hold the positions: historian I. Kh. Tkhamokova notes that «in 1589, soon after the town was built, 800 streltsy and Cossacks were to be sent there from Astrakhan, but the Astrakhan voivode sent only 600 men»(Citation: Терское казачество в этнокультурном пространстве Северного Кавказа 2017).

objects.description: The metropole's occupation administration abolished Nokhchi self-governance, forcibly subordinating them to an alien elite: historian E. N. Kusheva states that in 1614 Tsar Mikhail Fyodorovich ordered the Kabardian prince Sunchaley Yanglychevich Cherkassky «to be prince over all the Okochans... to judge them and to have charge of them in military organization and in all matters»(Citation: Народы Северного Кавказа и их связи с Россией (вторая половина XVI - 30-е годы XVII вв) 1963).

objects.description: The metropole's occupation administration abolished Nokhchi self-governance, forcibly subordinating them to an alien elite: historian E. N. Kusheva states that in 1614 Tsar Mikhail Fyodorovich ordered the Kabardian prince Sunchaley Yanglychevich Cherkassky «to be prince over all the Okochans... to judge them and to have charge of them in military organization and in all matters»(Citation: Народы Северного Кавказа и их связи с Россией (вторая половина XVI - 30-е годы XVII вв) 1963).

objects.description: The appointed administration forced the Indigenous population into unpaid labor: historian E. N. Kusheva points out that the Kabardian prince Sunchaley Yanglychevich Cherkassky compelled the service Okochans of the Terek town subordinate to him «to make all manner of wares for him, to plow the fields and to mow the hay»(Citation: Народы Северного Кавказа и их связи с Россией (вторая половина XVI - 30-е годы XVII вв) 1963). The metropole itself went years without paying for the military service of the Indigenous population: a report from the Terek voivode Pyotr Petrovich Golovin to the Astrakhan voivode Ivan Nikitich Odoyevsky records that they «serve the sovereign tsar... in all manner of the sovereign's Terek... services... yet have not been granted the sovereign's monetary and grain salary for the tenth year now»(Citation: Кабардино-русские отношения в XVI-XVIII вв. Документы и материалы. Том I 1957).

objects.description: The metropole's administration did not pay for forced labor and withheld food provisions for five years: a memorandum from the Posolsky Prikaz (Ambassadorial Office) to the Prikaz of the Kazan Palace records a complaint that the subordinate Okochans of Tersky Town «were not given the sovereign's grain allowance for the past years — for the 125th, and the 126th, and the 127th, and the 128th, and the 129th year»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

objects.description: The occupation administration deliberately exhausted the Indigenous population materially, forcing them to perform compulsory service at their own expense: in a petition submitted to Tsar Mikhail Fyodorovich, the Okotsky murza Kokhostrov Biytemirov and the serving Okochans of Tersky Town reported that, because their allowance went unpaid, they «were left without grain, have utterly perished from hunger and every hardship, have fallen, sovereign, into great debt, and are dying a death of starvation together with our wives and little children»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

objects.description: The occupation administration used the physical loss of documents to artificially lower the social status of local residents for the purpose of taxing them economically: an extract of the Posolsky Prikaz concerning a petition to Tsar Mikhail Fyodorovich states that after «the sovereign's charter of grant was lost», the heirs of the deceased Nokhchi delegate were stripped of their privileges and «made equal in everything with the Okochans, with the plowing people, and carts and wagons are exacted from them», whereas previously «no taxes whatsoever had been taken» from them(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

objects.description: The occupation administration and forces loyal to it sent the subordinate Nokhchi (Okochans) to take part in armed conflicts, including against their own compatriots: the historian I. Kh. Tkhamokova states that in 1626 the voivodes sent «252 Okochans»(Citation: Терское казачество в этнокультурном пространстве Северного Кавказа 2017)(Citation: Кабардино-русские отношения в XVI-XVIII вв. Документы и материалы. Том I 1957) on a campaign, and in 1628, during an armed incursion, the Kabardian murza Konshov-murza Bitemryukov «went against these “mountain people”... with the “Okochans”»(Citation: Терское казачество в этнокультурном пространстве Северного Кавказа 2017).

Tkhamokova states that in 1626 the voivodes sent «252 Okochans»(Citation: Терское казачество в этнокультурном пространстве Северного Кавказа 2017)(Citation: Кабардино-русские отношения в XVI-XVIII вв. Документы и материалы. Том I 1957) on a campaign, and in 1628, during an armed incursion, the Kabardian murza Konshov-murza Bitemryukov «went against these “mountain people”... with the “Okochans”»(Citation: Терское казачество в этнокультурном пространстве Северного Кавказа 2017).

objects.description: The occupation administration demanded that the Nokhchi mountain communities (the Shibutians) legally formalize their subordinate status: a report from the Terek voivodes Ivan Andreyevich Dashkov and Bogdan Gerasimovich Priklonsky to the Posolsky Prikaz records information about «the oath given by the Shibutians Lavarsan Yazyev and Zatyshka Lavarsanov on behalf of 20 households in 1627»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997), with a direct injunction that they «not fall away from the sovereign and remain under the sovereign's hand in outright bondage (kholopstvo)»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

objects.description: The occupation administration imposed an annual tribute in kind on the Nokhchi mountain communities (the Shibutians): a report from the Terek voivodes Ivan Andreyevich Dashkov and Bogdan Gerasimovich Priklonsky to the Posolsky Prikaz states that when subjecthood was formalized in 1627, the mountaineers were required «to give yasak at one kul (sack) of honey per year»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

objects.description: The metropole's occupation administration legally prohibited the free residence of the Indigenous population in Tersky Town, organizing the forced expulsion of unapproved persons and total demographic control: in 1631, Tsar Mikhail Fyodorovich issued a decree to the Prikaz of the Kazan Palace ordering a census of the newly arrived Nokhchi (Michkizians and Okochans) and ruling that those of them «who cannot be trusted» must be «ordered to be expelled out of Tersky Town, and ordered to go back whence each had come»(Citation: Кабардино-русские отношения в XVI-XVIII вв. Документы и материалы. Том I 1957); to ensure surveillance, in the state register of serving people for the region of the Prikaz of the Kazan Palace for 1637, the central authorities recorded in detail the number of subordinate residents of Tersky Town, including 350 «Okotsky people» and 680 newly arrived «Okochans, and Tatars, and Michkizians, and Shibutians»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997); and in 1640, on the orders of the Terek voivode, the Terek syn boyarsky P. Lukin and the clerk F. Belkov compiled a name-by-name register of the population of the Terek slobodas, rigidly recording every household of the subordinate Nokhchi (Okochans)(Citation: Кабардино-русские отношения в XVI-XVIII вв. Документы и материалы. Том I 1957)(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

objects.description: The metropole's occupation administration legally prohibited the free residence of the Indigenous population in Tersky Town, organizing the forced expulsion of unapproved persons and total demographic control: in 1631, Tsar Mikhail Fyodorovich issued a decree to the Prikaz of the Kazan Palace ordering a census of the newly arrived Nokhchi (Michkizians and Okochans) and ruling that those of them «who cannot be trusted» must be «ordered to be expelled out of Tersky Town, and ordered to go back whence each had come»(Citation: Кабардино-русские отношения в XVI-XVIII вв. Документы и материалы. Том I 1957); to ensure surveillance, in the state register of serving people for the region of the Prikaz of the Kazan Palace for 1637, the central authorities recorded in detail the number of subordinate residents of Tersky Town, including 350 «Okotsky people» and 680 newly arrived «Okochans, and Tatars, and Michkizians, and Shibutians»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997); and in 1640, on the orders of the Terek voivode, the Terek syn boyarsky P. Lukin and the clerk F. Belkov compiled a name-by-name register of the population of the Terek slobodas, rigidly recording every household of the subordinate Nokhchi (Okochans)(Citation: Кабардино-русские отношения в XVI-XVIII вв. Документы и материалы. Том I 1957)(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

objects.description: The occupation administration handed out privileges and transferred to loyal Nokhchi leaders power over dependent people in order to win them over to its side: the register of cases of the Posolsky Prikaz for 1645 records a petition from the serving Okotsk murza Chepan Kokhostrov to Tsar Mikhail Fedorovich and a report extract by the central apparatus «on granting him an increase to his salary and possession of the uzdens and «people» of his brother, murza Albir Kokhostrov»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

objects.description: The occupation administration forced the mountain societies of the Nokhchi into legal subordination: in 1647, under pressure from the Terek voivodes, the Shibutians «placed themselves under thy sovereign high hand in direct servitude... and swore the shert oath on the Quran»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997), while the Michkiz people «with all the Michkiz land placed themselves in servitude under thy sovereign high hand... and swore the shert on the Quran»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

objects.description: The occupation administration used the taking of hostages from among the Indigenous population to guarantee the loyalty of the mountain societies of the Nokhchi: a dispatch from the Terek voivode Prince Venedikt Andreevich Obolensky and his associates to the Posolsky Prikaz in 1647 officially records the fact of «the giving of an amanat to the Terek town»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997); the metropole instructed the voivodes «to order that amanats be taken from them — kinsmen of notable people»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997), as a result of which the Highlanders «gave a good amanat to the Terek town, Kasa»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997)(Citation: Народы Северного Кавказа и их связи с Россией (вторая половина XVI - 30-е годы XVII вв) 1963).

objects.description: The occupation administration dispatched emissaries to collect strategic, demographic, and economic data on the mountain societies of the Nokhchi: in 1658 the central apparatus of the Posolsky Prikaz instructed the Terek voivodes to find out «how many of them there are and what kind of people they are... and what fighting force they have... and what grows in their land, and what craftsmen there are»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997), in execution of which in 1659 the Terek voivodes Melenty Kvashnin and his associates «sent a streltsy commander into the Shibut land and ordered him to inspect in the Shibut land... the towns and places»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997), who, in an extract for the report of the Posolsky Prikaz to Tsar Alexei Mikhailovich of 1660, reported that «[to]wns they have none, nor any fighting forces»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

objects.description: The occupation administration made attempts to force the independent societies of the Nokhchi (the Shibutians) into legal subordination: an extract for the report of the Posolsky Prikaz to Tsar Alexei Mikhailovich of 1660 states that the Terek voivodes Melenty Kvashnin and his associates sent a military emissary to the Highlanders and ordered him «to bring them to the oath»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997); however, the attempt proved unsuccessful, and he «did not br[in]g the inhabitants of the Shibut land to the oath»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

objects.description: The occupation administration set itself the task of extracting hostages from the mountain societies of the Nokhchi (the Shibutians), but the attempt did not succeed: in 1658 the central apparatus of the Posolsky Prikaz directly instructed the Terek voivodes «to order that amanats be taken from them — kinsmen of notable people»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997), after which the Terek voivodes Melenty Kvashnin and his associates ordered their military emissary «to take an amanat to the Terek»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997); however, the extract for the report of the Posolsky Prikaz to Tsar Alexei Mikhailovich of 1660 records no handover of new hostages and merely states the old fact that «on the Terek [there is an amanat] of theirs»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

objects.description: The occupation administration of the Tsardom of Muscovy maintained the regime depriving the subordinated societies of the Nokhchi (the Okochans) of autonomy, officially formalizing the transfer of power over them to a new feudal lord loyal to the metropole: in 1661 Tsar Alexei Mikhailovich issued a charter of grant to the Kabardian prince Kaspulat Mutsalovich Cherkassky, instructing him «to be prince over the Okochans and over the Cherkas who serve us, the great sovereign, on the Terek, and to administer and judge them in military organization and in all our affairs»(Citation: Русско-чеченские отношения. Вторая пол. XVI-XVII в. 1997).

objects.description: The central authorities of the Tsardom of Muscovy used an appointed ruler for the legal subordination of the region: in 1676 the Posolsky Prikaz sent an instruction to the Kabardian prince Kaspulat Mutsalovich Cherkassky on the necessity of arriving at the Terek town «to administer the oath of the population of the North Caucasus to Tsars Ivan and Peter Alekseevich»(Citation: Кабардино-русские отношения в XVI-XVIII вв. Документы и материалы. Том I 1957).

objects.description: The appointed controlled administration sent subordinated Nokhchi (Okochans) to take part in the metropole's Crimean campaigns: a dispatch from the Kabardian prince Kaspulat Mutsalovich Cherkassky to the Posolsky Prikaz in 1675 states that for the campaign against the Crimean ulusy he had at his disposal «190 Okochan men»(Citation: Кабардино-русские отношения в XVI-XVIII вв. Документы и материалы. Том I 1957); the historian I. Kh. Tkhamokova adds that in 1675 detachments fought in Crimea alongside the prince «with uzdens, with the newly baptized, and with «Okochans»»(Citation: Терское казачество в этнокультурном пространстве Северного Кавказа 2017).

objects.description: The appointed controlled administration sent subordinated Nokhchi (Okochans) to take part in the metropole's Crimean campaigns: a dispatch from the Kabardian prince Kaspulat Mutsalovich Cherkassky to the Posolsky Prikaz in 1675 states that for the campaign against the Crimean ulusy he had at his disposal «190 Okochan men»(Citation: Кабардино-русские отношения в XVI-XVIII вв. Документы и материалы. Том I 1957); the historian I. Kh. Tkhamokova adds that in 1675 detachments fought in Crimea alongside the prince «with uzdens, with the newly baptized, and with «Okochans»»(Citation: Терское казачество в этнокультурном пространстве Северного Кавказа 2017).

objects.description: The occupation administration sent subordinated Nokhchi (Okochans) to take part in armed conflicts (the Chyhyryn campaigns) on the territory of Ukraine: the historian I. Kh. Tkhamokova notes that in 1678 the Kabardian prince Kaspulat Mutsalovich Cherkassky (under whose authority the Okochans were) received a tsar's charter «for having taken part in the Crimean and Chyhyryn campaigns»(Citation: Терское казачество в этнокультурном пространстве Северного Кавказа 2017); the document registers for 1678 record a dispatch from the Chuhuiv voivode Ivan Rykhtarov to the Razryadny Prikaz «on the march of the regiment of Prince Kaspulat Mutsalovich Cherkassky to Chuhuiv»(Citation: Кабардино-русские отношения в XVI-XVIII вв. Документы и материалы. Том I 1957); and in 1679 Tsar Fedor Alekseevich issued a decree to the Posolsky Prikaz «on his regiment performing guard duty in the vicinity of Chuhuiv and Kharkiv»(Citation: Кабардино-русские отношения в XVI-XVIII вв. Документы и материалы. Том I 1957).

Akhmadov states that in 1691–1700 «punitive expeditions were carried out by the tsarist authorities in retaliation against the rebel Cossacks and their Highlander allies»(Citation: Чечено-русские отношения в XVIII веке. objects.description: The government of the Tsardom of Muscovy organized attacks on the territories of the Nokhchi for the mass capture of prisoners and booty: historian Ya. Z. Akhmadov states that in 1718 there took place a "predatory expedition of detachments of Don Cossacks and Kabardian princes allied with Peter I into the 'Chechen uezd' along the Sunzha and the Argun"(Citation: Чечено-русские отношения в XVIII веке. Исследования и материалы. Том I 2019), as a result of which "800 prisoners were captured, not counting 'belongings'"(Citation: Чечено-русские отношения в XVIII веке. Исследования и материалы. Том I 2019), and in 1721 the Astrakhan governor A. P. Volynsky "invited the Don Cossacks and, together with the Terek Cossacks, organized raids to the Agrakhan and Aksai rivers against the Kumyks and Chechens"(Citation: Чечено-русские отношения в XVIII веке. Исследования и материалы. Том I 2019).

objects.description: The government of the Tsardom of Muscovy organized attacks on the territories of the Nokhchi for the mass capture of prisoners and booty: historian Ya. Z. Akhmadov states that in 1718 there took place a "predatory expedition of detachments of Don Cossacks and Kabardian princes allied with Peter I into the 'Chechen uezd' along the Sunzha and the Argun"(Citation: Чечено-русские отношения в XVIII веке. Исследования и материалы. Том I 2019), as a result of which "800 prisoners were captured, not counting 'belongings'"(Citation: Чечено-русские отношения в XVIII веке. Исследования и материалы. Том I 2019), and in 1721 the Astrakhan governor A. P. Volynsky "invited the Don Cossacks and, together with the Terek Cossacks, organized raids to the Agrakhan and Aksai rivers against the Kumyks and Chechens"(Citation: Чечено-русские отношения в XVIII веке. Исследования и материалы. Том I 2019).

objects.description: The Regular Army of the Russian Empire dispatched armed contingents to preemptively suppress an anti-colonial uprising: historian Ya. Z. Akhmadov cites a report by General Douglas, who ordered that the assembled rebel force must, «not being allowed to multiply, be averted and destroyed by the dispatched detachment»(Citation: Чечено-русские отношения в XVIII веке. Исследования и материалы. Том I 2019), after which, as historian Sh. B. Akhmadov states, «on July 4, 1732, the tsarist authorities dispatched a military detachment to Chechnya, headed by General Douglas, who commanded the troops at the Holy Cross fortress»(Citation: Чечня и Ингушетия в XVIII - начале XIX века 2002).

objects.description: The occupation administration of the Russian Empire imposed on the Indigenous population the legal codification of subordinate status, exploiting their economic need and presenting the oath as a rigid ultimatum: historian Ya. Z. Akhmadov states that in 1747, in response to the highlanders' requests for resettlement, «official consent of the imperial court was given («to admit and assign») on the condition that the highlanders take an oath of Russian subjecthood»(Citation: Чечено-русские отношения в XVIII веке. Исследования и материалы. Том I 2019), while to those absent «officers were sent «to administer the oath»»(Citation: Чечено-русские отношения в XVIII веке. Исследования и материалы. Том I 2019); similarly in 1748, when the mountain communities petitioned for subjecthood so that «traveling with merchandise to the town of Kizlyar... under protection would be free»(Citation: Чечено-русские отношения в XVIII веке. Исследования и материалы. Том I 2019), the administration «agreed to this proposal on the condition of the mandatory resettlement of the «Chebutlins» from the mountains to the lower reaches of the Sunzha»(Citation: Чечено-русские отношения в XVIII веке. Исследования и материалы. Том I 2019).

objects.description: The occupation administration of the Russian Empire imposed on the Indigenous population the legal codification of subordinate status, exploiting their economic need and presenting the oath as a rigid ultimatum: historian Ya. Z. Akhmadov states that in 1747, in response to the highlanders' requests for resettlement, «official consent of the imperial court was given («to admit and assign») on the condition that the highlanders take an oath of Russian subjecthood»(Citation: Чечено-русские отношения в XVIII веке. Исследования и материалы. Том I 2019), while to those absent «officers were sent «to administer the oath»»(Citation: Чечено-русские отношения в XVIII веке. Исследования и материалы. Том I 2019); similarly in 1748, when the mountain communities petitioned for subjecthood so that «traveling with merchandise to the town of Kizlyar... under protection would be free»(Citation: Чечено-русские отношения в XVIII веке. Исследования и материалы. Том I 2019), the administration «agreed to this proposal on the condition of the mandatory resettlement of the «Chebutlins» from the mountains to the lower reaches of the Sunzha»(Citation: Чечено-русские отношения в XVIII веке. Исследования и материалы. Том I 2019).

objects.description: The occupation administration of the Russian Empire stripped the Indigenous population of the status of a legitimate adversary by applying an inversion of meanings: historian Ya. Z. Akhmadov states that lawful defense was labeled with criminal terms, and «The anti-colonial and anti-feudal uprisings of the population of Chechnya, referred to in official documents as 'mischief', 'robberies', and 'murders', were perceived by the Russian autocracy as a challenge and an insult»(Citation: Чечено-русские отношения в XVIII веке. Исследования и материалы. Том I 2019), which served as a formal pretext for punitive actions.

objects.description: The apparatus of the Russian Empire constructed an image of the Indigenous population as savages: historian Ya. Z. Akhmadov points out that pre-revolutionary historiography described the highlanders' struggle as «the actions of barbarians devoid of 'civilized' notions of independence and freedom»(Citation: Чечня и Ингушетия в XVIII - начале XIX века 2002), while the imperial historian and participant in the events V. A. Potto cites the words of General A. P. Yermolov, who declared that «the cruelty of the local mores cannot be tamed by mercy»(Citation: Кавказская война. В 5 томах. Том 2. Ермоловское время 2007). In his «Notes», General Yermolov wrote of the Nokhchi: «the Chechens, the most vicious of the brigands, attacking the line», their land a refuge where «the villains of all other peoples, abandoning their own land on account of some crimes, were received amicably», while Chechnya itself «may justly be called the nest of all brigands», «were less filled than others with brigands who had previously taken part in all the raids of the Chechens on the line. In them predators gathered and took cover…»(Citation: Записки А.П. Ермолова. 1798-1826 гг. 1991).

objects.description: The propaganda apparatus of the Russian Empire used poetry to broadcast the logic of domination into society: the imperial historian and participant in the events V. A. Potto records that the poet A. S. Pushkin proclaimed in verse the inevitability of subjugation: «Submit, Caucasus - Yermolov is coming!»(Citation: Кавказская война. В 5 томах. Том 2. Ермоловское время 2007), while the poet V. A. Zhukovsky extolled the destruction of infrastructure by military commanders: «Scarcely at the villages - the villages blaze»(Citation: Кавказская война. В 5 томах. Том 1. От древнейших времен до Ермолова 2006).

objects.description: The Russian Empire, through the commander-in-chief in the Caucasus, General Gudovich, addressed the elders of the Nokhchi with a proclamation offering economic benefits in exchange for accepting subjecthood and ceasing armed resistance. For submission, the elders were promised access to salt: they would be “permitted to take salt from the local salt lakes by tickets, irrevocably, paying a very small fixed price,” as well as the right “to drive livestock to this side of the Terek and freely use the vacant pasture lands.” The proclamation was conveyed to Chechen society and its elders (Kusu Al-Temir, Masarai, Idut), but subjecthood was not accepted; at the beginning of the following year the empire proceeded to armed invasion.(Citation: Акты собранные Кавказскою археографическою комиссиею. Том III (1806-1809) 1869). The same offer is independently recorded by the imperial historian Dubrovin: the commander-in-chief in the Caucasus, General Gudovich, “promised… to release salt in unlimited quantity, for the most trifling payment; to permit the driving of livestock for pasture in wintertime to the left bank of the Terek River… and, finally, to make them equal to Russian subjects”(Citation: История войны и владычества русских на Кавказе. Том 5 1871).

objects.description: The Russian Empire sent troops into the lands of the Nokhchi in order to force its way deep into Greater Chechnya and break the resistance of its communities. The historian D. A. Khozhaev describes General Bulgakov's troops as having “come with fire and sword to the Chechen land,” and the Khankala battle of 1807 as bloody(Citation: Чеченцы в Русско-Кавказской войне 1998). In February 1807, three detachments under the overall command of the commander of the Caucasus Line, General Bulgakov, crossed the Terek; on February 13, the troops broke through the Khankala Gorge by storm, which the inhabitants had fortified with barricades, ditches, and abatis. The commander of the Caucasus Line, General Bulgakov, reported that he had entered “for the exemplary punishment” of the Nokhchi communities, that the inhabitants, having gathered in number about 10,000, “resolved to perish rather than let the Russian troops pass through the gorge”; during the storming of the gorge, of the defending Chechens, according to his report, there were “about 1,000 killed on the spot”(Citation: Акты собранные Кавказскою археографическою комиссиею. Том III (1806-1809) 1869). The imperial historian Potto admits that after Bulgakov's storming of the Khankala Gorge, Russian attempts to penetrate deep into Chechnya “were never renewed”(Citation: Кавказская война. В 5 томах. Том 2. Ермоловское время 2007).

objects.description: The Russian Empire sent troops into the lands of the Nokhchi in order to force its way deep into Greater Chechnya and break the resistance of its communities. The historian D. A. Khozhaev describes General Bulgakov's troops as having “come with fire and sword to the Chechen land,” and the Khankala battle of 1807 as bloody(Citation: Чеченцы в Русско-Кавказской войне 1998). In February 1807, three detachments under the overall command of the commander of the Caucasus Line, General Bulgakov, crossed the Terek; on February 13, the troops broke through the Khankala Gorge by storm, which the inhabitants had fortified with barricades, ditches, and abatis. The commander of the Caucasus Line, General Bulgakov, reported that he had entered “for the exemplary punishment” of the Nokhchi communities, that the inhabitants, having gathered in number about 10,000, “resolved to perish rather than let the Russian troops pass through the gorge”; during the storming of the gorge, of the defending Chechens, according to his report, there were “about 1,000 killed on the spot”(Citation: Акты собранные Кавказскою археографическою комиссиею. Том III (1806-1809) 1869). The imperial historian Potto admits that after Bulgakov's storming of the Khankala Gorge, Russian attempts to penetrate deep into Chechnya “were never renewed”(Citation: Кавказская война. В 5 томах. Том 2. Ермоловское время 2007).

objects.description: The Russian Empire dispatched troops to the lands of the Nokhchi to compel submission. The plan of the commander-in-chief in the Caucasus, General Gudovich, was to strike the unprotected: to catch the inhabitants before “their livestock and families… are sheltered in the mountains,” for “then… their punishment and complete success in the matter would be surer and more convenient.” When the commander of the Caucasus Line, General Bulgakov, delayed by an expedition in Dagestan, gave the inhabitants time to fortify the Khankala Gorge and took it by a bloody storm, General Gudovich, in a directive of March 20, 1807, refused to take this “on his own account” and stressed that he had not sent him to wage war: “you were sent not to wage war with the Chechen peoples, but to punish them and bring them into complete submission.” The commander of the Caucasus Line, General Bulgakov, considered the outcome of the campaign to be that the Chechens had by force of arms been “brought to such a state that they will long feel the blow dealt to them and, certainly, will not soon regain strength”(Citation: Акты собранные Кавказскою археографическою комиссиею. Том III (1806-1809) 1869).

objects.description: The Russian Empire compelled the Nokhchi communities by force of arms to swear an oath of subjecthood. After the devastation of the villages, the commander of the Caucasus Line, General Bulgakov, presented the Chechen people with a resolution by which the elders declared: “we submit ourselves with the whole Chechen people… into eternal loyal subjecthood… in witness whereof we give an oath according to our custom on the Holy Quran,” and for any violation the people subjected itself “to the strictest punishment and to the devastation of our dwellings without resistance”; the commander-in-chief in the Caucasus, General Gudovich, reported that the Chechens had been “completely subdued by force of arms and brought to an oath of eternal fidelity of subjecthood”(Citation: Акты собранные Кавказскою археографическою комиссиею. Том III (1806-1809) 1869).

objects.description: The Russian Empire held hostages from among the Nokhchi inhabitants as a guarantee of submission. Under the resolution presented by the commander of the Caucasus Line, General Bulgakov, the Chechen elders undertook: “we give the foremost among us as amanats, at the choice of the Russian commander in this region”; the villages of Bolshaya Ataga, Malaya Ataga, and Gekhi “gave 3 amanats from the best families,” whom the commander-in-chief in the Caucasus, General Gudovich, ordered “to send to Kizlyar… to keep watch over them and to issue for their maintenance 10 r. per month each”(Citation: Акты собранные Кавказскою археографическою комиссиею. Том III (1806-1809) 1869).

objects.description: The Russian Empire bought the loyalty of Nokhchi elders in order to use them to bring recalcitrant villages into subjecthood. The commander-in-chief in the Caucasus, General Gudovich, instructed the Andreyevo elder Hadji-Redjeb to incline the villages “into submission and subjecthood,” and assigned a salary to the Chechen uzden Bik-Bulat — “I persuaded the Chechen uzden Bik-Bulat… to whom I said… a salary of 300 r. in silver per year”; for winning over the remaining villages, “about 3,000 r. in silver for bringing them into loyal subjecthood” was allocated(Citation: Акты собранные Кавказскою археографическою комиссиею. Том III (1806-1809) 1869). The same bribery, from the Nokhchi side, is recorded by the historian D. A. Khozhaev: through the intermediary Hadji-Redjeb, in the name of the commander-in-chief in the Caucasus, General Gudovich, the very head of the Chechen resistance, Beibulat Taimiev, was won over and took “an oath of fidelity of subjecthood to Russia,” while Hadji-Redjeb asked the generals for another 3000 rubles in silver “for bringing the remaining unpacified Chechen villages into loyal subjecthood”(Citation: Чеченцы в Русско-Кавказской войне 1998).

objects.description: The Russian Empire set neighboring Indigenous peoples against one another so that their mutual enmity would weaken the resistance of each and prevent them from uniting. For the 1807 campaign against the Chechens, the commander-in-chief in the Caucasus, General Gudovich, coerced Kabardians into marching against the Nokhchi: for failure to appear, those “designated from the ranks of uzdens and begauls” faced a fine “of 50 r. in silver and 2 oxen.” General Delpozzo reported that he had “inclined the Kabardians to set out on the campaign and to assist together with our troops in punishing the Chechens,” and although “it was very difficult to persuade them,” he gathered over 3,500 men who “crossed the Terek River and arrived… at the Sunzha River” against the Chechen and Karabulak villages; at the same time, the Kabardians themselves refused to go directly “against the Chechens,” as their co-religionists, agreeing to act only “against the Karabulaks alone.” General Gudovich stated the aim of this incitement outright — “to set these two peoples at odds with each other and bring them into enmity against one another, and thereby weaken them over time”(Citation: Акты собранные Кавказскою археографическою комиссиею. Том III (1806-1809) 1869).
